questions.question_text: In how many ways can $5$ people stand in a line if $2$ particular people must NOT stand next to each other?

options.why: Calculated the number of arrangements where the two people DO stand together.
Calculated total unrestricted arrangements $5!$ without separating the pair.
Divided $120$ by $2$ assuming half of all arrangements separate the pair.

questions.question_text: How many arrangements of the $6$ letters in $\text{PLANET}$ have the vowels $\text{A}$ and $\text{E}$ separated?

options.why: Calculated the number of arrangements where $\text{A}$ and $\text{E}$ are adjacent.
Calculated the total unrestricted permutations $6!$ without separating vowels.
Divided $720$ by $2$ assuming half of all permutations have separated vowels.

questions.question_text: Three-letter words are formed without repetition from the letters of $\text{JOURNEY}$. How many contain $\text{J}$?

options.why: Calculated the complement, ${^{6}P_{3}} = 120$, counting words without $\text{J}$.
Calculated total unrestricted words ${^{7}P_{3}} = 210$.
Divided $210$ by $2$, incorrectly assuming half the words contain $\text{J}$.

questions.question_text: How many arrangements of the letters of $\text{OCEAN}$ have first two positions that are not both vowels?

options.why: Calculated only the unacceptable arrangements, $3 \times 2 \times 3! = 36$.
Calculated total unrestricted arrangements $5! = 120$.
Used $3 \times 3! = 18$ for the unacceptable count, forgetting the $2$ choices for the second vowel.

questions.solution_text:
Total $= 5! = 120$.
Both first positions are vowels $= 3 \times 2 \times 3! = 36$.
Acceptable $= 120 - 36 = 84$.

questions.question_text:
A panel of $3$ distinct roles (Leader, Recorder, Presenter) is chosen from $7$ candidates.
If Maya and Sam cannot both serve on the panel, how many panel arrangements are possible?

options.why: Calculated the unacceptable count where both Maya and Sam serve on the panel.
Calculated total unrestricted panel arrangements ${^{7}P_{3}}$.
Divided total panel arrangements in half incorrectly.

questions.question_text: In how many ways can $6$ people line up if Oliver cannot stand at either the front or the back of the line?

options.why: Calculated the unacceptable arrangements where Oliver is at an end.
Calculated total unrestricted arrangements $6!$.
Subtracted $5!$ for only one end position instead of both ends.

questions.solution_text:
Total $= 6! = 720$.
Oliver at either end $= 2 \times 5! = 240$.
Acceptable $= 720 - 240 = 480$.

questions.question_text: In how many ways can $9$ people stand in a line if neither Ava nor Max can stand at either end?

options.why: Used $9! - 4 \times 8!$, forgetting to subtract the overlap from the unacceptable count.
Calculated total unrestricted arrangements $9!$.
Calculated only the unacceptable arrangements, $4 \times 8! - 2 \times 7!$.

questions.solution_text:
Total $= 9! = 362880$.
Ava at either end $= 2 \times 8! = 80640$.
Max at either end $= 2 \times 8! = 80640$.
Both at the ends (counted twice) $= 2 \times 7! = 10080$.
Unacceptable $= 80640 + 80640 - 10080 = 151200$.
Acceptable $= 362880 - 151200 = 211680$.

questions.question_text:
$9$ students try out for a $3$-person executive committee (President, Vice-President, Secretary).
If Dan and Eva refuse to serve together, how many committee assignments are possible?

options.why: Calculated the unacceptable count where both Dan and Eva serve together.
Calculated total unrestricted committee assignments ${^{9}P_{3}}$.
Divided total committee assignments by $2$.
